title: BNP Paribas and microfinance: 25 years shared history
description: Committed for a long time into microfinance, BNP Paribas diversifies the initiatives through which its employees and clients can become involved by bringing a financial support or by providing their skills in the service of Microfinance Institutions, all around the world. Alain Lévy, Microfinance and Social Entrepreneurship Officer for Americas and Asia at BNP Paribas, presents to us the different levers for action implemented by the Group, as well as its principal operators.

asr.full_text: The commitment of BNP Paribas to microfinance is a longstanding commitment. We have been in the microfinance sector for over 25 years, notably with the first micro-credit given to the Crédit Rural de Guinée in 1989, then with a partnership which began in 1993 with the first French microfinance institution called ADI. Then, in the 2000s, the BNP Paribas Executive Committee, therefore at the highest level, decided to create a micro-finance cell which has since been integrated into the Department of CSR, Social and Environmental Responsibility, BNP Paribas. So we did it in Africa, we did it in Luxembourg, Italy, for example, so we are directly involved in the strategy of the microfinance institution. This is a role that is much more active. We are also going to help microfinance funds that have coverage. Which is very large in terms of geography, which can run to 50, 60, and so we are also going to run in countries where BNP has not been geographically implanted. BNP Paribas or BNP Paribas customers to buy shares in funds that are. BNP Paribas that are dedicated to microfinance for social entrepreneurship and so they will be able to help these institutions elsewhere that BNP Paribas already helps. The microfinance actors and specialists within the group, outside the people of the CSR, are all business bodies because we will rely on the risks that have helped us to build a credit policy for microfinance. on the country-aiders or the people of coverage, whether financial or corporate, that allow us to implement microfinance policy on a local basis. And we will also rely on volunteers, whether active or retired, to provide advice on specific topics to help microfinance institutions.

The discussion of microcredit activity, support for microfinance institutions, and employee expertise is informational, and the mention of customers buying shares in microfinance funds includes no stated guaranteed return, urgent payment demand, credential request, or deceptive outcome.
